claim_verdicts.evidence: 25.1 SQL Dump presents pg_dump as a utility producing a file with SQL commands that rebuild the database; 25.2 File System Level Backup is the alternative 'copy the files that PostgreSQL uses to store the data'. The lesson's contrast matches the two chapters.

25.1: "the dump represents a snapshot of the database at the time pg_dump began running." 13.2.1: Read Committed "is the default isolation level"; "two successive SELECT commands can see different data, even though they are within a single transaction". 13.2.2: Repeatable Read "sees a snapshot as of the start of the first non-transaction-control statement in the transaction". Lesson says 'as under Repeatable Read' (behaviour), not that pg_dump sets that level; supported. Round 2.

pg_dump options: "-F format / --format=format" with value "c / custom": "Output a custom-format archive suitable for input into pg_restore... allows manual selection and reordering of archived items during restore." 25.1: "A custom-format dump is not a script for psql, but instead must be restored with pg_restore". pg_restore -t: "Restore definition and/or data of only the named table."

25.1: "it does not dump information about roles or tablespaces (because those are cluster-wide rather than per-database)"; "Cluster-wide data can be dumped alone using the pg_dumpall --globals-only option." pg_dumpall -g: "Dump only global objects (roles and tablespaces), no databases." --no-role-passwords: "Do not dump passwords for roles" (so passwords are dumped by default).

Ledger now uses round-1 suggested_text. 25.1: "pg_dump does not block other operations on the database while it is working. (Exceptions are those operations that need to operate with an exclusive lock, such as most forms of ALTER TABLE.)" pg_dump -j: "If another client then requests an exclusive lock on a table, that lock will not be granted but will be queued... Consequently any other access to the table will not be granted either and will queue after the exclusive lock request."

Each pg_dump's dump is "a snapshot of the database at the time pg_dump began running" (25.1). backup-logical.sh at stage-3 runs the five pg_dump calls sequentially in one for loop (lines 18-21), so each snapshot starts later than the previous one; cross-database disagreement follows.

Script comment lines 7-8: "One directory per run in the backups volume (/backups in the lab box): not inside db's own volume, but still on this one machine." docker-compose.yml@stage-3 lines 30-33 mount backups:/backups separately from db-data. RPO = interval between runs follows from the course's RPO definition.

git show stage-3:scripts/devops/backup-logical.sh lines 7-26 match the lesson block character-for-character. git show stage-3:outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/backup-logical.txt matches the output block exactly (6 echo lines, 7 files listed, 'customers 5'). db/seed.sql inserts customers ids 1-5. (Round 1; S5 code block unchanged in rounds 2 and 3.)

Lines 13-14: "The lab databases that scripts rebuild (donhang_perf, donhang_tenancy, the shards...) are left out." Lines 31-37: count_rows runs pg_restore --data-only --table on donhang.dump for orders order_items customers, written to counts.txt; lines 39-43 print the listing. Ledger range 28-43 now correct; lesson wording 'reads three tables back out of donhang.dump with pg_restore' matches.

docker-compose.yml@stage-3: "From stage-3 Keycloak keeps its data, the realm's signing keys included, in the keycloak database on db, not inside its container"; KC_DB_URL: "jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/keycloak". db/databases.sql creates keycloak and donhang_tofu.

Round 3: S5 dropped '(from template0)'; text matches the narrowed ledger. pg_restore -d: "Connect to database dbname and restore directly into the database." -t: "Restore definition and/or data of only the named table." Note: "pg_restore's -t flag does not include such subsidiary objects" (indexes). Examples: new database cloned "from template0 not template1, to ensure it is initially empty"; 'create an empty database' holds.

Lesson S6 now says 'a plain copy of its files is usable only when the server is shut down'. 25.2: "The database server must be shut down in order to get a usable backup. Half-way measures such as disallowing all connections will not work (in part because tar and similar tools do not take an atomic snapshot..., but also because of internal buffering within the server)." 'holds recent changes in its own memory' = internal buffering.

25.1.1: "all the users who own objects or were granted permissions on objects in the dumped database must already exist. If they do not, the restore will fail to recreate the objects with the original ownership and/or permissions." pg_restore -e: "The default is to continue and to display a count of errors at the end of the restoration." Lesson and ledger now limit it to a server where role donhang was never created.

Line 9: dir="/backups/logical/$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%S)"; line 10: mkdir -p "$dir". One-second resolution; lesson S7 now says 'runs started at different seconds never overwrite each other', which holds.

Round 3: S5 now says 'make the script run itself again inside the lab box'. backup-logical.sh:4-5: "Everything below runs inside the lab box; this line puts it there." then [ -f /.dockerenv ] || exec .../lab-run.sh "$0" "$@", i.e. the script re-executes itself in the lab container. lab-run.sh:18 docker compose exec -T lab; up.sh:2 starts the lab box; docker-compose.yml:33 backups:/backups.
